title: Gateway refund amount is checked on an unlocked intent and sent to the provider before the row lock, so concurrent refunds exceed the paid amount
lower_trust_principal: Staff user holding payments.refund (or an idempotency-less retry/duplicate click from the UI)
boundary_crossed: Refundable-amount invariant (sum(refunds) <= intent.amount) and folio credit balance

entrypoint.description: POST /api/v1/payments/intents/{intent}/refunds validates only amount min:1 and calls PaymentService::refund with an unlocked PaymentIntent

sink.description: driverOf($intent)->refund(...) sends money back through MTN/Orange/card BEFORE the transaction and lockForUpdate at line 256-257; after the lock no re-check of refunded_amount is done

propagation.description: refundable check uses $intent->refunded_amount read without lock
folio credit check uses stale $folio->balance
FolioService::refund re-checks balance on the stale Folio instance passed in, then post() locks the folio only when writing
refunded_amount incremented after the fact

intended_control: amount <= intent.amount - refunded_amount and refund <= folio credit balance
observed_or_expected_result: Two simultaneous refund requests of the full refundable amount both pass the checks, both call the provider refund API, both post a refund line; the hotel refunds up to 2x the payment and the folio goes into debit.
conditions: two requests in flight concurrently (no Idempotency-Key header or different keys)
real gateway credentials configured (otherwise dry-run refund succeeds too)
smallest_fix: Open the DB::transaction and PaymentIntent::lockForUpdate() first, re-read refunded_amount and Folio::lockForUpdate()->balance inside it, insert the PaymentRefund row as pending, then call the gateway; mark succeeded afterwards.
regression_test_idea: Feature test spawning two parallel refund requests (or calling refund() twice inside a transaction with a sleep hook) for an intent of 10000 with amount 10000; assert only one PaymentRefund row and refunded_amount == 10000.

title: PayoutService::process reads pending MoMo items without any lock, so two concurrent /process calls disburse each salary twice
lower_trust_principal: Staff user holding payments.payouts (or UI double-submit / retry)

sink.description: $driver->disburse($item, ...) called for every item still 'pending' in the unlocked collection fetched at line 97-98; status update at line 111 happens after the provider call

propagation.description: items selected with plain ->get(), no lockForUpdate, outside a transaction
only postPaid() locks the run, after the money has already left

intended_control: item.status transitions pending -> sent/succeeded exactly once; attempts counter
observed_or_expected_result: Both workers see the same pending items and call MtnDisbursement/OrangeDisbursement twice per employee; the second update overwrites the first provider_reference. Salaries are paid twice; GL posts once.
conditions: two concurrent requests (no Idempotency-Key)
MoMo credentials configured (in dry run the duplicate is only visible in logs)
smallest_fix: Wrap process() in DB::transaction with PayoutRun::lockForUpdate() (or a cache lock per run) and re-select items with lockForUpdate(); mark an item 'sent' with its reference before calling the provider.
regression_test_idea: Two parallel process() calls against a run with one pending MoMo item and a fake gateway counting disburse() calls; assert exactly one call.

title: One payments.payouts user can reject a bank/cash payout item, rewrite its destination to any string and re-run it (no four-eyes, no audit event)
boundary_crossed: Employee bank/MoMo destination is HR master data (changed only via HR or an approved self-service request)

entrypoint.description: PUT /api/v1/payments/payouts/{payout}/items/{item} validates destination as free string max:60

sink.description: updateDestination() writes destination/channel on the item and re-queues it; bankFile() (line 123) and process() (line 94) then pay to it

propagation.description: rejectPayoutItems lets the same user move any pending bank/cash item to 'failed' first
no SoD check, no comparison against Employee.bank_account/momo_number, no EventBus record
confirmPayout by the same user marks items paid and posts GL (empty item_ids confirms ALL)

intended_control: Salary destinations come from the employee record; sensitive changes go through HR approval (SelfService::decide)
observed_or_expected_result: Attacker rejects a colleague's bank item, sets destination to their own account/number, downloads the bank CSV or processes the MoMo item; salary is diverted. Only the payout_run row changes; no audit trail of the edit.
conditions: user has payments.payouts
payout run in pending/processing state
smallest_fix: Restrict updateDestination to the value currently on the Employee record (or require hr.manage + record an event with old/new), validate format per channel, and forbid reject+update by the run creator.
regression_test_idea: As payments.payouts user: reject item, PUT destination '999999999', assert 403/422 or that the stored destination still equals Employee.momo_number.

title: PosController::can() accepts pos.view for every write action: a read-only POS user can open checks, add items, settle and charge to any in-house guest folio
boundary_crossed: pos.manage write boundary (checks, settlement, room charges)

entrypoint.description: private can(): abort_unless(pos.manage || pos.view) used by store, addItem, fire, updateLine, removeLine, split, settle, chargeToRoom, sync, transfer, comp

sink.description: chargeToRoom posts charges to the guest folio via FolioService::charge (no folios.manage needed); settle (line 178) records payments

propagation.description: chargeToRoom calls $this->can() only
sync (offline batch) also only $this->can()

intended_control: pos.view = read-only; pos.manage required to write
observed_or_expected_result: A viewer account (e.g. auditor, trainee) can create checks and charge them to any checked-in reservation, or settle checks for cash without a cashier shift being theirs (settle requires an open shift only for cash/card/mobile kinds).
conditions: user has pos.view but not pos.manage
smallest_fix: Give can() an $ability argument like the other controllers and require pos.manage for all non-GET actions.
regression_test_idea: User with only pos.view POSTs /pos/checks and /pos/checks/{id}/charge-to-room; expect 403.

title: POS offline sync accepts negative/zero quantities and unvalidated payment arrays, letting a server lower a check total or settle with arbitrary methods/amounts
lower_trust_principal: Staff user with pos.view/pos.manage (no pos.void or pos.discount)

entrypoint.description: 'checks.*.items.*.quantity' => ['sometimes','numeric'] (no min); 'checks.*.payments' => ['nullable','array'] with no per-payment rules (compare addItem line 51 min:0.001 and settle line 110-112)

sink.description: addItem stores quantity and amount = round(price*qty) with negative qty; Check::recalculate (Domain/Check.php:52) sums amounts so the total drops; settle() only requires sum(payments.amount) == total

propagation.description: sync feeds each item straight to addItem
sync feeds raw payments to settle; negative 'amount' entries are accepted and stored in pos_payments (PosService 201-205)

intended_control: quantity >= 0.001; payments.*.amount integer min:1; voids/discounts need pos.void/pos.discount
observed_or_expected_result: A server syncs a check with lines [item A x1 = 5000, item A x-0.9 = -4500], total 500, settles for 500 cash and serves 5000 worth of goods (stock consumed by pos.check_settled items). Or settles [CASH 10000, CASH -9500] making the drawer expect 500.
conditions: user can reach POST /pos/sync (any pos.view/pos.manage user)
smallest_fix: Apply the same rules as addItem/settle inside sync ('quantity' min:0.001, 'payments.*.method' required string, 'payments.*.amount' integer min:1) and reject negative line amounts in PosService::addItem.
regression_test_idea: POST /pos/sync with an item quantity -1 and a payment amount -100; expect 422.

title: Folio transfer accepts any destination folio (including city-ledger folios) and negative amounts, bypassing the company credit-limit/approval check
boundary_crossed: Company credit billing approval (company.city_ledger) and credit_limit enforced only in transferToCityLedger

entrypoint.description: transfer validates 'amount' => ['required','integer'] (no min) and 'to_folio_id' any integer

sink.description: transfer() posts transfer_out/transfer_in to any two open folios regardless of kind; no check against from-folio balance

propagation.description: transferToCityLedger() has the credit_limit and city_ledger-approved checks that transfer() lacks
only amount === 0 or same folio is rejected

intended_control: Direct billing only to approved companies within credit limit; transfers move charges, not arbitrary credit
observed_or_expected_result: A guest's balance can be moved to an open city-ledger folio of a company that is not approved or already over its limit (receivable risk), and a negative transfer pulls credit from another guest's/company's folio onto the attacker's chosen folio, which can then be refunded (folios.adjust) or used to close the folio at check-out.
conditions: user has folios.manage
an open city_ledger folio exists for the company (created by any earlier direct bill)
smallest_fix: In transfer(): require amount > 0, forbid to->kind === 'city_ledger' (route those through transferToCityLedger), and optionally cap amount at from->balance for guest folios.
regression_test_idea: Transfer -5000 from folio A to B and transfer 5000 into a city-ledger folio of a company with credit_limit 1000; expect DomainException in both cases.

title: Folio refund validates the credit balance on the unlocked Folio instance; concurrent refunds exceed the credit

sink.description: if ($folio->balance > -$amount) uses the route-bound model; post() at line 238 locks the folio only to insert the line and increment

propagation.description: balance incremented after insert; no re-validation under lock

intended_control: Refund cannot exceed the credit balance
observed_or_expected_result: Two parallel refunds of a 10000 credit each pass the check; folio ends at +10000 debit and the cashier pays out 20000.
conditions: concurrent requests without a shared Idempotency-Key
smallest_fix: Move the balance check into post() (or re-fetch with lockForUpdate before checking) for type refund.
regression_test_idea: Concurrency test with two refunds on a folio with balance -10000; assert the second raises and final balance is 0.

title: accounting.post_manual posts journal entries that are marked approved_by the poster, and can reverse any system-generated entry (folio, payroll, stock) without a second person
boundary_crossed: Four-eyes on GL postings (PeriodLocking implements it for periods, nothing does for entries)

sink.description: approved_by stored from meta with no distinct-user check; reverse() at line 121 reverses any entry regardless of source_type

propagation.description: reverse endpoint only checks accounting.post_manual
core variant also sets approved_by to the actor
'journal' free-form string max:10 and any date in an open period accepted

intended_control: Preparer/approver separation for manual journals; subledger-driven entries corrected via their source document
observed_or_expected_result: One user can post Dr cash / Cr revenue adjustments or reverse the automatic Cr 411 / Dr treasury entry of a payment, making the GL disagree with folios and hiding cash shortages; approved_by shows them as approver.
conditions: user has accounting.post_manual
period open
smallest_fix: Do not set approved_by on post; add an approve step requiring a different user with accounting.approve (or at least record approved_by null and flag in reports); restrict reverse() to source_type manual/reversal.
regression_test_idea: Post a manual entry and assert approved_by is null; reverse a journal entry with source_type 'folio' and expect 422.

title: Payroll preparer check compares against prepared_by set at first compute; a second user can recompute with arbitrary bonus inputs and then approve as 'not the preparer'
lower_trust_principal: Staff user holding payroll.manage and payroll.approve (or payroll.approve alone after any colleague created the draft)
boundary_crossed: Segregation of duties between payroll preparation and approval

entrypoint.description: POST /payroll/runs recompute with 'inputs.*.bonuses' integer min:0 (no max), per employee

sink.description: approve() only refuses when prepared_by === actor; prepared_by is set once by firstOrCreate at line 51 and never updated on recompute

propagation.description: recompute deletes and rebuilds all payslips with the new inputs, prepared_by unchanged
bonuses/service_charge flow straight into net

intended_control: The payroll must be approved by someone other than the preparer (sod)
observed_or_expected_result: User A creates the draft; user B (approver) recomputes with bonuses => 5,000,000 for themselves and approves immediately; GL posts and the run becomes payable via PayoutService.
conditions: two users exist; approver also has payroll.manage (common 'HR manager' role)
smallest_fix: Set prepared_by (and last_computed_by) on every compute and refuse approval if either equals the actor; cap bonus inputs or require review when inputs change.
regression_test_idea: A computes, B recomputes with inputs, B approves -> expect DomainException 'sod'.

title: hr.manage / payroll.manage / talent.requests users can change their own employee salary, bank or MoMo destination, grant themselves advances and approve their own self-service change request
lower_trust_principal: Staff user who is also an employee and holds hr.manage, payroll.manage or talent.requests
boundary_crossed: Self-dealing on compensation data (LifecycleService::assertSod exists for compensation changes but not for these paths)

entrypoint.description: PATCH /hr/employees/{employee}: base_salary, bank_account, momo_number, payment_method with no check that $employee->user_id !== actor

sink.description: base_salary feeds proratedBase; PayoutService::create (Payouts/PayoutService.php:49-53) pays to employee.bank_account/momo_number

propagation.description: grantAdvance: payroll.manage can create a SalaryAdvance for any employee including themselves (no SoD, no limit)
decideRequest -> SelfService::decide (SelfService/SelfService.php:82) applies bank_change/momo_change with no requester != decider check
contrast: compensation changes DO enforce assertSod (requester and subject)

intended_control: Sensitive changes (address, phone, bank, MoMo) are requests that HR decides; compensation changes require a different approver
observed_or_expected_result: An HR manager raises their own base_salary or redirects their payout destination directly; a talent.requests holder approves their own bank_change request; a payroll.manage user grants themselves a loan that the next payroll only partially recovers.
conditions: actor's user is linked to an Employee row in the same hotel
smallest_fix: Reuse LifecycleService::assertSod semantics: abort when $employee->user_id === actor id for updateEmployee (salary/bank fields), grantAdvance and SelfService::decide.
regression_test_idea: User linked to employee E with hr.manage PATCHes own base_salary; expect 403/422.

title: loyalty.adjust_points can credit an unlimited number of points in one call; points are cash-equivalent via folio/POS redemption
lower_trust_principal: Staff user holding loyalty.adjust_points (+ loyalty.manage or pos access to redeem)
boundary_crossed: Loyalty liability (419800) created without a sale

entrypoint.description: POST /loyalty/members/{member}/adjust validates points integer not_in:0, reason string; no max, no 4-eyes

sink.description: credit() adds the points; redeemOnFolio (line 141) converts them to a PTS folio payment and PosLoyalty::redeemTender (PosLoyalty.php:55) to a POS tender

propagation.description: positive branch has no cap and no lock

intended_control: Manual adjustments should be bounded and/or approved
observed_or_expected_result: Staff credits 1,000,000 points to an accomplice member, who pays a folio or bar check with points; revenue is offset against loyalty liability that never corresponded to earned points.
conditions: user has loyalty.adjust_points
smallest_fix: Add a per-adjustment cap (program setting) above which a second approver is required; record adjustments to the EventBus with actor for alerting.
regression_test_idea: Adjust +10,000,000 points as a single user; expect 422 above the configured cap.

title: DryRunGateway reports every intent as 'succeeded' on status poll; any public pay/deposit status request settles the folio without money whenever APP_ENV is not exactly 'production' or the intent was created as dry_run
lower_trust_principal: Anonymous guest holding a manage-booking token or a pay-link URL
boundary_crossed: Folio payment posted only on confirmed provider settlement

sink.description: status() returns 'succeeded' for any intent; PaymentService::settle then posts the folio payment (PaymentService.php:224-231)

propagation.description: driverFor falls back to DryRun whenever the hotel has no credentials and app()->isProduction() is false (APP_ENV='staging','prod','local'...)
driverOf returns DryRun for any intent with driver='dry_run' even in production
same pattern for disbursements

intended_control: Dry run only for development; production refuses unconfigured gateways
observed_or_expected_result: On a live deployment whose APP_ENV is e.g. 'staging' or 'prod' (or a hotel onboarded before credentials were set), a guest starts a pay-link payment and polls status: the deposit/folio is credited and deposit_paid incremented with no funds received.
conditions: APP_ENV !== 'production' on an operational instance, or an intent created while the hotel had no credentials
smallest_fix: Gate DryRunGateway on an explicit config flag (payments.allow_dry_run) that defaults false, and refuse to settle a dry_run intent when the flag is off.
regression_test_idea: With APP_ENV=staging and no credentials, create an intent and poll status; expect 'pending'/failure, not a folio line.

title: Approved data-protection requests anonymise the guest row, register entries, company contacts and activity log, but guest names/contacts persist in folios, invoices, payment intents, pay links and online check-ins
lower_trust_principal: Guest exercising erasure; any later staff reader of those tables
boundary_crossed: Erasure/anonymisation promise (PrivacyService header: 'only personal fields are blanked')

entrypoint.description: anonymise() updates guests, guest_register_entries, company_contacts, activity_log only

sink.description: folios.name is built from guest full_name and is never blanked; invoices.bill_to_name/address copy it at line 216-218

propagation.description: payment_intents.payer_phone / payer_email kept indefinitely
payment_links.payer_phone kept
online_checkins (id_type, document data) not touched by anonymise
reservations.special_requests/notes free text about the guest remain

intended_control: Personal fields blanked across modules; financial amounts kept
observed_or_expected_result: After approval the guest still appears by name in folio lists, invoices, payment-intent searches (payer_phone ilike), pay links and online check-in records; erasure is partial and the audit entry claims full anonymisation.
conditions: guest had a stay with folio/invoice/online payment
smallest_fix: Extend anonymise() to blank folios.name, invoices.bill_to_name/address (where company_id is null), payment_intents.payer_*, payment_links.payer_phone, online_checkins and reservation free-text for the guest; add a retention job for payer contact data on settled intents.
regression_test_idea: Create guest with reservation, folio, invoice and intent; approve a delete request; assert none of those rows contain the original name/phone/email.

title: Employee has no $hidden; employees index/show return bank_account, momo_number, cnps_number, tax_number, base_salary and allowances to hr.view and payroll.manage holders
lower_trust_principal: Staff user holding hr.view (e.g. department supervisors)
boundary_crossed: Need-to-know for payment destinations and government identifiers

entrypoint.description: GET /hr/employees returns Employee models paginated (full toArray)

propagation.description: showEmployee loads contracts (salary history) too
can('view') accepted for hr.view and payroll.manage

intended_control: SelfService::profile masks bank_account/momo_number even for the employee themselves (SelfService.php:48-55)
observed_or_expected_result: Any hr.view user can export every colleague's bank account and MoMo number (useful for social engineering a payout diversion) and salary.
conditions: user has hr.view
smallest_fix: Add an Employee API resource (or $hidden for bank_account, momo_number, cnps_number, tax_number) and expose those fields only to hr.manage/payroll.manage via an explicit endpoint.
regression_test_idea: hr.view user GETs /hr/employees; assert response lacks bank_account and momo_number.

title: General-ledger report loads every journal line of an account for an arbitrary date range into memory with no cap

entrypoint.description: validate from/to only as dates; no max span

sink.description: ->get() of all journal_lines for the account between from and to, then PHP loop computing running balance

propagation.description: trialBalance/incomeStatement aggregate in SQL (safe); generalLedger does not

observed_or_expected_result: Repeated requests for account 411100 from 2000-01-01 to 2100-01-01 on a busy hotel (tens of thousands of lines/month) exhaust worker memory/time; 1200/min api limit does not help.
conditions: large journal_lines table
user with accounting.view
smallest_fix: Cap the range (e.g. 366 days) and paginate or stream lines with a cursor.

title: FolioService::open consumes the gapless folio number outside a transaction, so the row lock is released immediately and concurrent opens collide on the unique (hotel_id, number) index
lower_trust_principal: Two staff users / online payments opening folios at the same time

entrypoint.description: NumberSequence::next() called from Folio::create outside DB::transaction (contrast invoice() line 201 which wraps it)

sink.description: lockForUpdate() in autocommit mode: lock released after the SELECT, two callers read the same 'last'

propagation.description: unique(hotel_id, number) turns the duplicate into a 500 for one caller; guestFolioFor (FolioService:47) is also unlocked so two guest folios can be opened for one reservation
PosService::open has the same pattern for pos-check numbers (split() wraps it, open() does not)

intended_control: NumberSequence docblock: 'must run inside the caller's transaction'
observed_or_expected_result: Under load (night audit + online deposit settle + front desk), one of the concurrent folio creations fails with a unique-violation 500 or two open guest folios are created for the same reservation, splitting charges across folios.
conditions: concurrent folio/check creation for the same hotel
smallest_fix: Wrap open() (and PosService::open) in DB::transaction; in guestFolioFor lock the reservation row first.
regression_test_idea: Parallel open() calls x10; assert 10 distinct numbers and no exception.
